purpose: Ensures third parties who create, receive, maintain, or transmit ePHI on behalf of the covered entity are contractually bound to protect it.
summary: The covered entity may permit a business associate to create, receive, maintain, or transmit ePHI on its behalf only if the covered entity obtains satisfactory assurances, through a written contract or other arrangement, that the business associate will appropriately safeguard the information.
expectedStatementElements: How business associates are identified before ePHI is shared
What safeguard obligations are included in business associate agreements (BAAs)
How BAAs are tracked and kept current
What happens if a business associate violates its BAA obligations
How subcontractors of business associates are addressed
evidenceExamples: Inventory or register of active business associates and BAA status
Policy describing the BAA review and renewal process
Evidence of a BAA violation being addressed or terminated
commonGaps: No central inventory of who qualifies as a business associate
BAAs exist but are outdated or don't reflect current data flows
No process to confirm subcontractors of business associates also sign BAAs
No defined consequence or process when a business associate violates the agreement
interviewQuestions: How do you determine when a vendor needs a Business Associate Agreement?
Can you show me your current inventory of business associates and BAA status?
What happens if you find out a business associate isn't meeting its obligations?
How do you handle subcontractors that a business associate brings in?
